supporting_observations.claim: The periodic outbound HTTPS activity is consistently associated with update.stockpilot.com. Successful requests are logged at approximately 13:40:41, 13:45:59, 13:50:21, 13:55:20, 14:05:54, and 14:10:40 UTC; the 14:00:16 attempt received proxy status 407.

The network records tie these requests to C:\Program Files\StockPilot\stockpilotupd.exe (PID 4108), running as eli.brooks; the process start and outbound connection are directly recorded at 13:40, and subsequent firewall and Sysmon records identify the same process for the StockPilot connections.

The inventory identifies stockpilotupd.exe and update.stockpilot.com as approved software and service, with checks expected about every five minutes. The observed destination, process, and cadence are consistent with that approved activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show the requested hostname and tunnel metadata, but the successful StockPilot entries are logged as tunnels; these records do not show the HTTPS application payload or what was downloaded. Relevant examples: T206-00103, T206-00121, T206-00206.

The supplied records do not include a hash, signature verification, or other integrity validation for stockpilotupd.exe; they establish its path and process/network association, not that the binary is authentic. Relevant records: T206-00101, T206-00106.
claims_not_established: Whether the StockPilot updater binary was authentic and unmodified.
What content, if any, was exchanged inside the successful HTTPS tunnels.
Why the 14:00:16 proxy attempt required authentication or whether that attempt transferred any application data.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: a network authentication record names ruth.moss and WS-EBROOKS-01 as the originating workstation; a corresponding network logon appears on WS-RMOSS-01. This is outside the alerted periodic HTTPS activity and does not establish misuse by itself. Records: T206-00011, T206-00012.

Separate review: UserAssist registry writes contain encoded paths corresponding to mstsc.exe and powershell.exe. These entries do not, by themselves, prove execution or malicious use. Records: T206-00127, T206-00187.

Separate review: eli.brooks launched the Cisco AnyConnect UI, and a Cisco-signed module was loaded. The inventory says there is no VPN; these records do not show a VPN connection. Records: T206-00194, T206-00195, T206-00196.

Separate review: FILE-BLU-01 resolved WS-EBROOKS-01 and then connected to TCP port 9997 on it; the connection ended with RST. The records do not identify the service or establish whether this was expected. Records: T206-00283, T206-00285.
